relations.definition: Indicates that a person or thing is a participant or element in an event or activity.
relations.embedding_query_text: involves: Indicates that a person or thing is a participant or element in an event or activity.

chosen_property.label: participant
chosen_property.justification: participant fits all instances: events/missions/agreements have people or vehicles as participants.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

relations.definition: Indicates that something is employed as a means or tool for an action.
relations.embedding_query_text: uses: Indicates that something is employed as a means or tool for an action.

chosen_property.label: instrument
chosen_property.justification: instrument expresses the tool/means used by an action, matching launch/flight using a vehicle.

candidates.label: instrument
candidates.comment: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: recipe
candidates.comment: A recipe relation between a cook action and the specific recipe used as an instrument. Also called recipe used, instructions for, cooking guide. Examples: "A cook action uses the recipe 'Classic Lasagna'.", "Baking a cake uses the recipe 'Chocolate Fudge Cake'.", "Preparing dinner uses the recipe 'Chicken Stir-fry'."

candidates.label: language
candidates.comment: A communication medium relation between a communicate action or write action and the language employed in that action. Also called language used, medium of communication, spoken in, written in. Examples: A communicate action uses the language 'English'. A write action uses the language 'French'. A conversation has the language 'Spanish'. Distinct from inLanguage, which is for the language of a creative work itself, not the action of communicating/writing.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: actionProcess
candidates.comment: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

relations.definition: Indicates the location from which a vehicle or object is sent off.
relations.embedding_query_text: launched from: Indicates the location from which a vehicle or object is sent off.

chosen_property.label: fromLocation
chosen_property.justification: fromLocation indicates the origin place of an action, fitting launch from a cosmodrome.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: shippingOrigin
candidates.comment: The geographical region or location from which a shipment originates. Also called shipment source, origin of delivery, dispatch location. Examples: `Offer Shipping Details` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: California`, `Shipping Conditions` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: Warehouse A`, `International Shipment` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: China`. Distinct from `shippingDestination`, which is where the shipment goes.

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: dropoffLocation
candidates.comment: A drop-off location relation between a rental car reservation and the place where the rental car can be returned. Also called "return location", "car return point", "drop-off point". Examples: "Rental car reservation dropoffLocation 'Airport Terminal 2'", "Car rental dropoffLocation 'Downtown Office'", "Reservation dropoffLocation 'Hotel Parking Lot'".

candidates.label: pickupLocation
candidates.comment: A spatial attribute indicating the place where a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be collected. Also called collection point, pick-up point, embarkation point. Examples: A taxi reservation has a pickup location of 'Grand Central Station'. A rental car reservation has a pickup location of 'Airport Terminal 1'. The ride-share booking has a pickup location at 'Home Address'.

candidates.label: payload
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the maximum permitted weight of passengers and cargo a vehicle can carry, excluding the vehicle's own weight. Also called carrying capacity, load capacity, cargo weight limit. Examples: A truck has a payload of 1000 kg. A car has a payload of 500 kg. An aircraft has a payload of 20,000 lbs. Distinct from weight, which refers to the weight of the empty vehicle itself.

candidates.label: steeringPosition
candidates.comment: A specification of the steering wheel's position in a vehicle, typically for cars. Also called "steering wheel side", "driver's side", "left-hand drive", "right-hand drive". Examples: "The car has steeringPosition LeftHandDriving", "This vehicle's steeringPosition is RightHandDriving", "The steeringPosition indicates where the driver sits."

candidates.label: vehicleTransmission
candidates.comment: A vehicle transmission relation between a vehicle and the type of component used for transmitting power to the wheels. Also called transmission type, gearbox type, drivetrain. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".

candidates.label: aircraft
candidates.comment: An aircraft relation between a flight and the specific type of vehicle used for air travel. Also called airplane type, plane model, flight vehicle. Examples: "A flight's aircraft is 'Boeing 747'.", "The flight uses an 'Airbus A320'."

relations.definition: Indicates the date or day on which an event takes place.
relations.embedding_query_text: occurred on: Indicates the date or day on which an event takes place.

chosen_property.label: startDate
chosen_property.justification: startDate is the standard for when an event occurs; DayOfWeek is a valid date value.

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: exceptDate
candidates.comment: An exception date relation between a schedule and a specific date or datetime when a scheduled event will not take place. Also called: exclusion date, cancelled date, unavailable date. Examples: "Weekly Yoga Class Schedule" except date "2023-12-25", "Daily Bus Route Schedule" except date "2024-01-01T08:00:00", "Monthly Book Club Schedule" except date "2023-11-11".

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

relations.definition: Indicates the time or location at which an event takes place.
relations.embedding_query_text: occurred at: Indicates the time or location at which an event takes place.

chosen_property.label: timestamp
chosen_property.justification: timestamp gives the specific time of an event, matching launch/docking times.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

relations.definition: Indicates the place to which someone or something is going.
relations.embedding_query_text: destination: Indicates the place to which someone or something is going.

chosen_property.label: toLocation
chosen_property.justification: toLocation is the destination of an action, fitting launch to the space station.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: itinerary
candidates.comment: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: tripOrigin
candidates.comment: A trip origin relation between a trip and its starting location, prior to any destinations. Also called starting point, departure location, point of origin. Examples: "Flight tripOrigin 'London Heathrow Airport'", "RoadTrip tripOrigin 'New York City'", "Trip tripOrigin 'Home Address'".

candidates.label: arrivalBusStop
candidates.comment: An arrival bus stop relation between a bus trip and the station or stop where it concludes. Also called destination bus stop, final bus station. Examples: "A bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Grand Central Station'.", "The bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Main Street Stop'."

candidates.label: arrivalTerminal
candidates.comment: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.

candidates.label: departureStation
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.

candidates.label: arrivalStation
candidates.comment: A station where a train trip concludes. Also called: train destination, end station, terminal station. Examples: "TrainTrip 456 arrivalStation 'Grand Central Station'", "TrainTrip from Rome arrivalStation 'Termini Station'", "TrainTrip to Berlin arrivalStation 'Hauptbahnhof'". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which specifies the specific platform within a station.

candidates.label: departureBusStop
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a bus trip and the stop or station from which it departs. Also called: origin bus stop, departure bus station, bus departure point. Examples: "Bus Route 101" departure bus stop "Central Bus Station", "Intercity Bus" departure bus stop "Port Authority Bus Terminal". Distinct from arrivalBusStop, which is the destination stop.

candidates.label: deliveryAddress
candidates.comment: A destination relation between a parcel delivery and its destination postal address. Also called: shipping address, recipient address, delivery location. Examples: "Package" delivery address "123 Main St, Anytown, USA", "Food Order" delivery address "Apt 4B, 567 Oak Ave", "Mail" delivery address "P.O. Box 100".

relations.definition: Indicates that something is a component or member of a larger whole.
relations.embedding_query_text: part of: Indicates that something is a component or member of a larger whole.

chosen_property.label: subEvent
chosen_property.justification: subEvent expresses a launch as part of a larger mission.

chosen_property.label: memberOf
chosen_property.justification: memberOf indicates persons as members of an agreement.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

relations.definition: Indicates that one event or thing comes after another in time or sequence.
relations.embedding_query_text: follows: Indicates that one event or thing comes after another in time or sequence.

chosen_property.label: previousItem
chosen_property.justification: previousItem indicates the preceding item in a sequence, matching docking follows launch.

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: nextItem
candidates.comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: measuredProperty
candidates.comment: A measured property relation between an observation or statistical variable and the property being measured. Also called: property measured, observed characteristic, variable property. Examples: "Temperature Observation measuredProperty 'temperature'", "GDP StatisticalVariable measuredProperty 'Gross Domestic Product'", "Survey Response measuredProperty 'satisfaction level'". Distinct from variableMeasured, which is a broader property for describing what is measured in a dataset.

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: variableMeasured
candidates.comment: A variable measured relation between a dataset or observation and the variables that are measured within it. Also called measured variable, data variable, observation parameter. Examples: "Dataset variableMeasured 'Temperature'", "Observation variableMeasured 'Humidity'", "Dataset variableMeasured 'Patient Age'".

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: measurementQualifier
candidates.comment: A measurement qualifier relation between an observation or statistical variable and an enumeration providing additional qualification. Also called: observation qualifier, measurement attribute, data context. Examples: "GDP Observation measurementQualifier 'Nominal'", "Inflation Rate measurementQualifier 'Annualized'", "Population Count measurementQualifier 'Estimated'".

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

relations.definition: Indicates the year or time when a person first traveled in space.
relations.embedding_query_text: first flew in: Indicates the year or time when a person first traveled in space.

chosen_property.label: startDate
chosen_property.justification: startDate indicates the year of the first flight.

candidates.label: estimatedFlightDuration
candidates.comment: An estimated flight duration relation between a flight and the duration or text representing its approximate travel time. Also called "approximate flight time", "expected flight length", "scheduled flight duration". Examples: "Flight 'UA123' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT5H30M'", "Flight 'DL456' estimatedFlightDuration '6 hours'", "Flight 'LH789' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT10H'".

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: dateVehicleFirstRegistered
candidates.comment: A temporal registration relation between a vehicle and the date of its first registration with public authorities. Also called: first registration date, initial registration, vehicle registration date. Examples: "Car" date vehicle first registered "2018-03-15", "Motorcycle" date vehicle first registered "2020-07-01", "Truck" date vehicle first registered "2015-11-20".

candidates.label: copyrightYear
candidates.comment: A temporal relation between a creative work and the year its copyright was first asserted. Also called: year of copyright, copyright date, first copyright year. Examples: "Classic Album" copyright year "1970", "Software Version 1.0" copyright year "2005", "Research Paper" copyright year "2022". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first publication or broadcast.

candidates.label: flightDistance
candidates.comment: A flight distance relation between a flight and the total distance covered during its journey. Also called: journey distance, air travel distance, flight length. Examples: "Flight UA123" flight distance "1500 miles", "Flight BA456" flight distance "2400 km", "Flight LH789" flight distance "Long-haul".

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: yearBuilt
candidates.comment: A construction year relation between an accommodation and a number, indicating the year in which the accommodation was built. Also called construction year, built year, year of construction. Examples: Hotel yearBuilt 1985, ApartmentBuilding yearBuilt 2010, House yearBuilt 1950.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: arrivalTime
candidates.comment: An expected time of arrival for a trip. Also called: estimated arrival, scheduled arrival, landing time. Examples: "Trip to NYC arrivalTime '2023-10-27T14:30:00'", "Flight 789 arrivalTime '18:00'", "Bus Trip arrivalTime 'tomorrow 09:15'."

relations.definition: Indicates the vehicle or mission on which a person traveled in space.
relations.embedding_query_text: flew on: Indicates the vehicle or mission on which a person traveled in space.

chosen_property.label: aircraft
chosen_property.justification: aircraft indicates the vehicle used for flight, fitting Crew Dragon.

candidates.label: aircraft
candidates.comment: An aircraft relation between a flight and the specific type of vehicle used for air travel. Also called airplane type, plane model, flight vehicle. Examples: "A flight's aircraft is 'Boeing 747'.", "The flight uses an 'Airbus A320'."

candidates.label: flightDistance
candidates.comment: A flight distance relation between a flight and the total distance covered during its journey. Also called: journey distance, air travel distance, flight length. Examples: "Flight UA123" flight distance "1500 miles", "Flight BA456" flight distance "2400 km", "Flight LH789" flight distance "Long-haul".

candidates.label: estimatedFlightDuration
candidates.comment: An estimated flight duration relation between a flight and the duration or text representing its approximate travel time. Also called "approximate flight time", "expected flight length", "scheduled flight duration". Examples: "Flight 'UA123' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT5H30M'", "Flight 'DL456' estimatedFlightDuration '6 hours'", "Flight 'LH789' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT10H'".

candidates.label: payload
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the maximum permitted weight of passengers and cargo a vehicle can carry, excluding the vehicle's own weight. Also called carrying capacity, load capacity, cargo weight limit. Examples: A truck has a payload of 1000 kg. A car has a payload of 500 kg. An aircraft has a payload of 20,000 lbs. Distinct from weight, which refers to the weight of the empty vehicle itself.

candidates.label: flightNumber
candidates.comment: A flight number relation between a flight and its unique identifier, typically including the airline IATA code. Also called: flight ID, airline code, flight identifier. Examples: "Flight from London to New York" flight number "BA177", "Flight from Tokyo to San Francisco" flight number "UA838", "Flight from Sydney to Dubai" flight number "EK413".

candidates.label: mileageFromOdometer
candidates.comment: An odometer mileage relation between a vehicle and the total distance traveled as read from its odometer. Also called: odometer reading, total mileage, distance traveled. Examples: "Car mileageFromOdometer '50000 KMT'", "Truck mileageFromOdometer '120000 SMI'", "Motorcycle mileageFromOdometer '15000 km'".

candidates.label: callSign
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a broadcast service, person, or vehicle and its unique callsign. Also called "radio identifier", "station ID", "vehicle identifier". Examples: "Radio station broadcast service callSign 'KEXP'", "Amateur radio operator person callSign 'W1AW'", "Aircraft vehicle callSign 'N123AB'".

candidates.label: departureTerminal
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure terminal identifier. Also called: terminal number, flight terminal, departure building. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure terminal "Terminal 5", "Flight UA123" departure terminal "Terminal 3". Distinct from arrivalTerminal, which is the arrival terminal.

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

relations.definition: Indicates that a person gave a characterization or account of someone or something.
relations.embedding_query_text: described: Indicates that a person gave a characterization or account of someone or something.

chosen_property.label: description
chosen_property.justification: description is the general property for characterizing a person.

candidates.label: description
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a thing and its textual description. Also called: item description, details, explanation. Examples: "Product" description "A versatile smartphone with advanced camera features.", "Event" description "An annual conference for tech enthusiasts.", "Person" description "A renowned scientist and author.". Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription
candidates.comment: A clarifying description relation between a thing and a short text used to distinguish it from similar items. Also called: clarifying description, distinguishing text, unique description. Examples: "Apple" disambiguating description "The fruit, not the company.", "Mercury" disambiguating description "The planet, not the element.", "Jaguar" disambiguating description "The animal, not the car brand.". Distinct from description, which is a general description.

candidates.label: character
candidates.comment: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: mainEntityOfPage
candidates.comment: A main entity of page relation between a thing and the creative work or URL for which it is the primary described entity. Also called: primary page, described on page, featured on page. Examples: "Albert Einstein mainEntityOfPage Wikipedia Article", "The Election mainEntityOfPage News Report", "Quantum Physics mainEntityOfPage Research Paper". Distinct from mainEntity, which indicates the primary entity described in a creative work.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: characterAttribute
candidates.comment: An attribute relation describing a particular aspect of a fictional character within a game or video game series. Also called "character trait", "character property", "game attribute". Examples: "Video game character attribute 'Strength'", "RPG game character attribute 'Magic Resistance'".

candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.
